whatItIs.heading: What wildfire restoration means for Palisades Fire-affected homes
whatItIs.body: The Palisades Fire of January 2025 burned tens of thousands of acres across Pacific Palisades, Malibu, and adjacent communities—destroying structures outright and pushing smoke and ash into a far larger ring of surviving homes. Wildfire restoration in this context means two things. For homes with fire involvement: debris management, structural assessment, smoke remediation, and complete reconstruction. For the greater number of homes that survived but were exposed to smoke and ash: surface decontamination, HVAC system cleaning, content documentation, and air-quality verification using HEPA filtration equipment and clearance-level testing. Wildfire smoke carries compounds—volatile organic compounds, heavy metals, fine particulates—from burned structures across the Westside. These are not removed by standard cleaning. IICRC-trained technicians and professional-grade equipment are required to bring interior environments back to safe, measurable standards.

process.heading: How Gallagher supports Pacific Palisades homeowners after the Palisades Fire

steps.title: On-site assessment and written scope
steps.body: The crew arrives within 60 minutes of dispatch from our Southern California operations and evaluates structural condition, smoke and soot distribution, HVAC contamination, exterior ash load, and contents. The written assessment is submitted directly to your insurance carrier.

steps.title: Containment and exterior decontamination
steps.body: Exterior ash is cleared from rooflines, gutters, vent intakes, and decking before it migrates further indoors. HVAC systems are isolated to stop circulating contaminated air. Containment barriers separate affected zones from clean areas inside the home.

steps.title: Smoke, soot, and odor remediation
steps.body: Interior surfaces are cleaned by method appropriate to the material: dry sponge for light deposits, chemical cleaning for heavier soot. Thermal foggers and hydroxyl generators neutralize odor compounds embedded in framing and porous finishes. HEPA air scrubbers run until clearance readings are confirmed.

steps.title: Reconstruction and insurance documentation
steps.body: For structurally damaged Palisades homes, Gallagher manages the full rebuild under one project management contact: framing, drywall, insulation, roofing coordination, flooring, cabinetry, paint, and fixtures. Documentation runs throughout—photo logs, written scope, and line-item cost records for the adjuster file.

signs.heading: Situations that call for professional restoration in Pacific Palisades
signs.intro: If your home was in the Palisades Fire region, professional assessment is appropriate even when the structure is visually intact.

items.title: Smoke odor that does not clear after days of ventilation
items.body: Persistent odor means smoke compounds have bonded to insulation, drywall, wood framing, and soft furnishings. Ventilation alone cannot reverse this; targeted treatment with appropriate cleaning agents and odor neutralization equipment is required.

items.title: Ash or soot visible on interior surfaces
items.body: Wildfire ash infiltrates through gaps around windows, doors, and HVAC intakes. It contains heavy metals and chemical compounds from burned residential and commercial structures. Spreading it with household cleaning methods increases exposure.

items.title: HVAC system operated during or immediately after the fire
items.body: Any system running while ash was airborne has pulled contamination through the entire duct system. The full system—air handler, supply lines, return lines, and filter housing—must be cleaned and cleared before it runs again.

items.title: Structural fire damage to the home
items.body: Burned roofing, charred siding, compromised framing, or heat-damaged windows all require structural assessment before interior work begins. Gallagher coordinates with structural engineers and LA County permitting as needed.

items.title: You have an insurance estimate but no contractor in place
items.body: Gallagher can take over restoration at any stage—including after another company has done mitigation or an adjuster has issued an estimate. A free on-site visit confirms whether the existing scope matches conditions on the ground.

pricing.heading: Palisades Fire restoration pricing for Pacific Palisades homeowners
pricing.body: Restoration costs split along the same lines as the fire itself. Smoke and ash remediation for a home that survived the Palisades Fire but requires professional decontamination—surfaces, HVAC, air-quality verification—typically ranges from $1,500 for a smaller intrusion to $10,000 or more for a larger home with significant contamination. Structurally damaged homes requiring partial reconstruction start around $15,000. Full rebuilds after major structural fire involvement can run $50,000 to well above that for larger Westside properties. Gallagher Restoration Co. provides a free on-site assessment: no charge to arrive, document, and produce a written scope for the insurance carrier. Get that assessment before signing any restoration contract—documented scope is the foundation of a successful wildfire insurance claim.

faqs.q: Does my homeowners insurance cover Palisades Fire smoke damage if my home did not burn?
faqs.a: Most standard California homeowners policies cover wildfire smoke and soot damage, including homes that were not in the direct burn path. Coverage specifics depend on your policy language. Gallagher Restoration Co. produces written documentation from day one and coordinates directly with your adjuster throughout the claim process.

faqs.q: How long does Palisades Fire smoke remediation take in a typical home?
faqs.a: Smoke-only remediation in a typical Pacific Palisades home takes three to seven days depending on square footage, the severity of contamination, and how many surfaces require treatment. HVAC decontamination adds time. Structural restoration timelines depend on the extent of fire damage and LA County permitting requirements.

faqs.q: My Pacific Palisades home was outside the direct burn area. Is professional remediation still necessary?
faqs.a: If you notice persistent smoke odor, visible ash or soot on surfaces, or indoor air symptoms when spending time inside the home, professional assessment is warranted. Smoke and fine ash from the Palisades Fire traveled well beyond the burn perimeter and infiltrated homes through standard gaps in the building envelope.
